findings.description:
Des encryption algorithm is vulnerable to attacks. The DES (Data Encryption Standard) was designed by the National Bureau of Standards (NBS) in 1976 and has been widely used for symmetric-key data encryption since then. However, it has several weaknesses that make it susceptible to certain types of attacks, including brute-force attacks, chosen plaintext attacks, and related key attacks. These vulnerabilities can be exploited by attackers who have access to the encrypted data or who know the encryption parameters. The DES algorithm is considered weak because it uses a 56-bit key, which is significantly shorter than the recommended 128-bit key length for modern cryptographic standards. While it may still provide some level of security in certain applications, it is no longer recommended for new implementations due to its vulnerabilities and ease of attack.

For more details on this issue, please refer to Data Encryption Standard.
findings.recommendation: Use a stronger encryption algorithm such as AES (Advanced Encryption Standard) or GCM (Galois/Counter Mode).
